get.description: Liveness + database check, used by Docker Compose and Caddy.

post.description: Send a 6-digit login code by SMS (locally: written to the server console).
Check the code and start a session (about 60 days). The account is created on first login.

get.description: Who is logged in. Also sets the CSRF cookie, so the app calls it first, before the login form.

post.description: Register a company; the logged-in person becomes its owner. A wrong code creates nothing.

get.description: Pending invitations for the logged-in phone number, from any company.

post.description: Join the location. Works only for the invited phone number; anyone else gets 404.

get.description: All invitations of a location, newest first (the manager sees who has not answered yet).

post.description: Invite a person by phone number. No SMS is sent; they see the invitation after logging in.

get.description: The manager's start screen: every location they run, the state of its current period and who is missing.

post.description: A new location starts with the good-practice rules switched on (or follows its group's rules).

patch.description: Name, address, group, period length, default deadline; archiving (owner only) instead of deleting.

post.description: Enter a free-access code. Extends access from its current end date; works also after it has expired.

patch.description: Move the availability deadline (the day the manager will arrange the schedule).

post.description:
"Poproś o dyspozycje": an in-app notice with the period and the deadline for every active employee of the
location (or only those who have not finished). Nothing is arranged automatically: the manager arranges the
schedule when the deadline has passed or everyone has answered.
Start arranging schedules, one run per location. Answers at once; poll `GET /generation-runs/{id}`.

get.description: My published shifts from today on, who works with me, and my hours per month. Works in read-only mode.
One version of a location's schedule: the grid, the three scores, rules, unmet requests and history.

Why this shift has its person (or nobody), and what each person with the position would change.
Quick checks with the validator, no solver; the same list is the manual editor's choice of people.

post.description: Validate a manual change before saving it (e.g. while dragging): new problems and the new scores.

patch.description: Save a manual change (one shift, or two for a swap). Refused with the reasons when it breaks a hard rule.

post.description: Pin (or unpin) the person on a shift: arranging the schedule again keeps pinned people in place.
Correct a published schedule: a new draft copy (or the newest draft, if there already is one).
Publish the newest draft: employees see it in "Mój grafik"; the previous version stays as history.

get.description: My availability for a period; without `period_id`, the nearest period that is collecting availability.

put.description: Save the marked days (saved at once after every tap or drag; "Cofnij" sends the previous states).

post.description: "Powtarzaj co tydzień do [data]": the chosen weekdays get this state from the period start until that date.
"Skopiuj z poprzedniego miesiąca": each day takes the state of the same weekday 4-5 weeks earlier.
"Gotowe": tells the manager I have finished. Days left unmarked mean "mogę".
"Coś jeszcze?": a request in words for things the calendar cannot say. Only managers read it.

delete.description: Take back my own request while the period is still collecting availability.

get.description: Employees × days of the period: what each person marked, who finished, what changed after the deadline.
Requests in words for this period, oldest first. Only managers see them.

patch.description: The manager rejects a request, or marks it as more or less important than usual.

get.description: Everything the location settings screen shows.

delete.description: Also removes its staffing; refused when a schedule already uses it (history stays intact).

patch.description: New hours apply to schedules arranged from now on; saved schedules keep the hours they had.

delete.description: Removes its staffing too. Saved schedules keep their shifts (with the hours copied).

put.description:
The whole weekly table at once: how many people of each position every shift needs on each weekday.
Cells with 0 (or left out) mean nobody.

post.description: A different staffing on one date (e.g. Christmas Eve), replacing the weekday's for that shift and position.

get.description: People whose home location this is: active first, then switched off; by surname.

patch.description: Positions, experience level, monthly maximum and target, or switching the person off (history stays).

put.description:
Save the whole list. In a location, a rule set exactly like in the group (also its place) keeps following
the group; anything else becomes the location's own setting.

post.description:
What the change would mean on the last schedule of each location, checked without arranging it again
(the generator runs only in the background).

get.description: Hours of published shifts in a month, per person and location (the locations this manager runs).
The same report as a CSV file (semicolons and decimal commas, so a Polish spreadsheet opens it as is).

post.description:
'Oddaj zmianę': everyone who could take my shift gets an in-app notification. It stays mine until the
manager approves someone.
The giver keeps the shift after all.

get.description: 'Zmiany do wzięcia': shifts given away in the company that I can take now (or already said 'Biorę' to).

post.description: 'Biorę': the managers of the location decide; the shift is not mine until they approve.

get.description: 'Oddane zmiany' in my locations: open ones, those waiting for my decision, and the last two weeks.

post.description: The volunteer gets the shift in the published schedule (checked by the validator again).

get.description: My newest notifications, newest first, and how many I have not seen. Works in read-only mode.

post.description: Mark my notifications as seen (not company data, so allowed in read-only mode too).

ErrorOut.description: Every error response: a plain-language Polish message that can be shown to the person as is.
ErrorOut.title: ErrorOut
